engineSelect.heading: Choose a Tradition, Then a Style
engineSelect.lead: Instead of showing every calculation engine at once, pick the sidereal tradition first. Each tradition explains where it comes from, then lets you choose the house style inside it.
engineSelect.guidanceStep2: 2. Pick the house style from its dropdown
engineSelect.guidanceStep3: 3. Generate the chart with that method
engineSelect.summaryImpactText: The ayanamsha shifts sidereal planet degrees; the house style changes how life areas are divided around the ascendant.

lahiri.label: Lahiri
lahiri.description: The most widely used modern Vedic ayanamsha. It is a calm default for natal readings, dashas, and broad client-facing reports.
lahiri.method: Lahiri anchors the sidereal zodiac to the traditional Chitra/Spica reference used in mainstream Indian panchang and ephemeris work.
lahiri.summary: Mainstream Vedic reference, best for general chart interpretation.

raman.label: Raman
raman.description: A comparative Vedic frame associated with Dr. B. V. Raman's school. It is useful when a practitioner wants a slightly different sidereal correction.
raman.method: Raman uses a separate precession offset from Lahiri, so planets and cusps can shift subtly near sign or house boundaries.
raman.summary: Comparative Vedic reference for practitioners checking alternate timing traditions.

krishnamurti.label: Krishnamurti
krishnamurti.description: The Krishnamurti Paddhati approach supports fine-grained predictive work, especially when paired with Placidus houses.
krishnamurti.method: KP combines its own ayanamsha with house cusps and sub-lord analysis, making it popular for event-focused readings.
krishnamurti.summary: KP-oriented reference for detailed prediction and event analysis.

whole_sign.label: Classic Whole Sign
whole_sign.description: Each sign becomes one complete house from the ascendant sign. This is the cleanest Vedic default.

equal.label: Equal Houses
equal.description: Each house is exactly 30 degrees from the ascendant degree. It keeps house sizes uniform.

placidus.label: Placidus
placidus.description: A time-based quadrant system popular in Western astrology and central to many KP workflows.

koch.label: Koch
koch.description: A birthplace-based quadrant system that emphasizes the ascendant's local rising motion.

campanus.label: Campanus
campanus.description: Divides the prime vertical into equal arcs, giving a spatial view of house division.

regiomontanus.label: Regiomontanus
regiomontanus.description: Uses equal divisions of the celestial equator, historically important in medieval astrology.

navamsa.heading: Navamsa (D9)
navamsa.introText: The Navamsa (D9) is the most important divisional chart in Vedic astrology. It reveals the soul's deeper purpose, the nature of marriage and partnerships, and the strength of planetary placements at a dharmic level. When a planet occupies the same sign in both the Rashi and Navamsa charts, it achieves Vargottama status — a mark of exceptional strength.
